title: Quiet launch pricing — first principles & back-of-envelope
content:
Goal: sketch a tiny, low-friction pricing surface for a small cohort (quiet launch, invite-only) focused on latency-sensitive interactive apps (chat widgets, copilots). Keep activation effortless but protect against outsized cost from heavy users.

Guiding constraints (first principles):
- Keep the first dollar experience low friction: minimal sign-up friction, small free credit to demonstrate value.
- Prefer simple mental models: 'minutes' or 'sessions' are easier for app PMs than raw tokens.
- Latency-sensitive users value predictability over tiny savings. Offer both payg and tiny commit.
- We must avoid gaming: credits that can be massively stacked and sold.

Key levers (what we can tune):
- Per-token unit price (hosted) by model class (small, medium, large).
- Session/minute credits vs token credits vs per-request units.
- Concurrency surcharge or standby fee for reserved slots (to avoid infinite websocket idle time).
- Burst buffer for brief peaks (free up to X per hour).
- Threshold-based escalator to nudge enterprise/contact-sales.

Tiny plan idea (invite-only starter):
- Free trial: $25 credit, 30 days.
- Starter payg: $10/mo + payg tokens. $10 acts as small commitment to reduce abuse.
- Default unit: "interactive-minute" (IM) approx = 1 minute of active conversation for a single concurrent user.
  - How to map IM -> tokens: assume average of 80 tokens/minute outbound + 20 tokens/minute inbound = 100 tokens/minute (conservative for short messages).
  - So 1 IM ≈ 100 tokens.
  - If using gpt-like model analog: cost to us per 1k tokens (hosted small model): say $0.03/1k tokens -> per IM cost = 100 tokens -> $0.003. But overheads, infra, routing, SLO provisioning -> multiply by 6x to cover infra + margin -> $0.018 per IM.
  - Starter retail price: charge $0.05 per IM (rounding up for simplicity). That yields gross margin cushion.

Back-of-envelope conversions (example numbers):
- Assumptions: average request length 150 tokens, average conversation density 100 tokens/minute, model class = medium, our blended infra and license cost = $0.12 / 1k tokens.
- Cost per token = $0.00012. Cost per IM (100 tokens) = $0.012. After infra allocation & OSS engineering amortization multiply 3x -> cost basis = $0.036.
- Retail target markup for starter = 2.0x -> price = $0.072 per IM.
-> But psychologically want simpler numbers: 5¢ or 7¢ per IM. Pick 5¢ for MVP to reduce friction.

Alternative: session bundles (good for copilots):
- Session = 10 IMs (assume 10 minute interactive session) -> sell bundles of 100 sessions = 1000 IMs.
- Price granularity: 1000 IMs @ $0.05 = $50 -> good clean pricing. Equivalent to ~100k tokens.

Burst protection / anti-abuse rules: (notes)
- Idle websockets: bill idle after 90s of inactivity at 0.01 IM/min (or charge per-second throttle).
- Concurrent connections > 10 per account require explicit opt-in or reserve slot add-on.
- If avg token/session >> assumed (e.g., embeddings-heavy), fall back to token-metered variant automatically.

Payg vs reserved small commits:
- Offer tiny monthly commit $40 / 800 IMs (implicit 5¢/IM). Developer psychology: commit feels cheap but signals intent.
- Include roll-over credits for 30 days only. Encourages steady usage.

Latency premium idea:
- Two product rails: 'fast' (reserved low-latency instances) vs 'standard' (multi-tenant batching).
- Fast adds 40% surcharge to IM price. For starter we could include 1 hour/month of fast credit to show UI -> converts.

Sample unit-econ quick calcs for a starter cohort (per 100 customers):
- Assumptions: 100 customers, each pays $40 commit/month -> ARR = 100 * $40 * 12 = $48k.
- Average active concurrent sessions per customer per day = 1.5, avg IM/day per customer = 60 -> monthly IMs/customer = 1800. That's large — starter cohort likely much less. Use conservative: 300 IMs/mo.
- 300 IMs * $0.05 = $15/mo revenue/customer -> 100 customers = $1,500/mo = $18k ARR.
- Cost basis (blended) = $0.012 per IM -> cost per customer = 300 * 0.012 = $3.6 -> gross margin high. But this underestimates infra overhead.

Edge-case pricing triggers (to auto-escalate to sales):
- Monthly spend > $1,000 -> contact enterprise.
- Sustained concurrency > 50 -> talk about Dedicated.
- Token spike > 1M tokens/day -> rate limit or invite to upgrade.

Open questions / to-do: 
- Need robust mapping from actual token counts to IM abstraction; instrumentation must show both.
- How to treat function calls/tooling which generate extra tokens? (charge delta tokens on top of IM).
- Billing cadence: monthly invoicing + immediate consumption notice. Consider prepaid first for quiet launch to reduce fraud.
- Free tier vs free credit: which better for funnel? Free credit is simplest.

Psych experiments / messaging notes: 
- Pricing copy: "5¢ per interactive minute (roughly 100 tokens) — perfect for chat widgets and copilots". Simple conversion line helps.
- Emphasize predictability + latency options. "Reserve low-latency slots for steady load".

Implementation checklist (engineering/product):
- [ ] Instrument IM metric in runtime (per-account IMs, IM->token conversion heuristic).
- [ ] Billing prototype: convert IM usage -> token-equivalent on invoice.
- [ ] Add idle billing timeout for websockets.
- [ ] UI: show 'estimated minutes left' prominently in dashboard.
- [ ] Metric: average tokens per IM across cohort; re-evaluate quarterly.

Notes to self: keep it simple for quiet launch. If adoption positive, iterate: add per-route pricing, latency premium split, and small reserved slots for teams. Avoid introducing too many levers that confuse early users.

Random brain dump numbers for later refinement: 
- GPU hour -> tokens conversion (rough): Llama2-medium-like serving throughput -> 1 GPU-hour yields ~20M generation tokens (very rough). So cost per 1k tokens at $1/gpu-hr -> $0.00005 - but with infra and infra ops multiply heavily. This is just sanity.
- If we think in tokens: 1000 IMs -> ~100k tokens -> cost base ~ $12 (depending on model).

Sign-off: draft for internal alignment. Next step: test wording in signup flow, prototype IM instrumentation, run a small cohort (<50 teams) for 4 weeks, gather real token->IM conversion.

Notes: keep copy terser for marketing later. For now this is a working notebook with rough numbers and TODOs.
